# Gateway and safety (area `gateway`)

Boundaries code enforces: confirmations, protection lists, terminal typing, redaction, secrets and the sealed fill path, owner identity.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **GATE-1** (agent): FERB's launchd definitions (the user LaunchAgent plists and FERB.app's BUNDLE_SERVICE) are FERB_SERVICE, never lifted; the shell profile denies writing them. A daemon not run from FERB.app (from ~/.ferb/venv or a checkout) also protects the installed FERB.app (/Applications, then ~/Applications, with FERB's bundle id) like the bundled one: never written or removed by FERB's tools or shell, its service definition counted as FERB's. Read at daemon start.
- **GATE-2** (agent): OwnerSecrets.delete deletes the Keychain item through the signed helper that made it (its delete operation: SecItemDelete by service and account), never reading it first; an item not found counts as deleted, and an item another entry still names stays. It is journaled secret.deleted with place and name only. secrets.saved shows place, name and kind, never a value, Keychain account or username.
- **GATE-200** (owner): For the escape hatch and the file tools, one read question per protected folder per task covers every read of that folder in the task. Writes and admin still ask per command.
- **GATE-201** (agent): The foreground Need is keyed by confirm.app_key: the running app's bundle id (casefolded) when the name, `pid:N` or bundle id names exactly one running app, else the argument without case or invisible marks. The question shows the app as the worker wrote it. One Yes covers every spelling and retry in the task.
- **GATE-202** (owner): Tools report structural facts (a form submit and its action host, card/password field types, the checkout amount on the page, the recipient a mail/message tool uses); facts raise the question. The worker's `effect` declaration can only add a question, never remove one.
- **GATE-203** (owner): File tools are bound by the never-read and never-write protection lists, like the shell. A task that needs a listed place asks the owner: reads once per protected folder per task (GATE-200), writes per action.
- **GATE-204** (owner): Asked once when the final amount is known, with amount and merchant read from the page by code (never the worker's number; if unreadable, the question says so). The Yes covers that payment in this task's tab and what it opens until it completes or 10 minutes pass; another tab or task asks again. A bank page whose amount or merchant differs asks again showing both; an OTP question repeats them. With no bank page, it asks at the final pay click; a changed amount asks again. Known sites never skip it.
- **GATE-205** (owner): Recipients and sites the owner approved stay known for good. Sites mentioned in a request are known for normal use in that and later tasks; only sending private data there after outside content was read still asks once.
- **GATE-206** (owner): Card fields (autocomplete cc-number / cc-csc / cc-exp) are secret fields like password and OTP fields: values never captured in snapshots, boxes masked in screenshots; card details are filled only through the sealed path (stored once in the Keychain) or the site's / browser's saved card. The redactor masks CVV beside its label and expiry beside a card. Storing a card works like other owner secrets: asked, hidden input, models see only a handle.
- **GATE-207** (owner): One "don't ask for 30 minutes" answer covers routine questions only: the foreground question, protected-folder read lifts, a browser's own pages, new recipients and profile pairing. It never covers payments, account security, permanent deletion, terminal typing, certificate checks turned off or the sink question. The window is one value for the gateway, spanning tasks until it ends; Yeses inside it record destinations like normal Yeses.
- **GATE-211** (agent): All reviewed OTP rules are kept (email layouts, markup, backup-code lists).
- **GATE-212** (agent): Card numbers are checked (Luhn) over every window of digit groups, so `qty 2 <card>` is caught. Expiry is masked only in MM/YY form after an expiry label or right after a card; CVV only beside its label (or after a card and expiry).
- **GATE-214** (agent): A submitted form with a card field (cc-number/cc-csc/cc-exp) asks as a payment. A current-password field together with a new_password field asks as account security; a sign-up's new-password field alone asks nothing. A tool's `deletes` outside the Trash ask as permanent delete of each path (counted first if a folder). Each fact kind is decided with its own target and provenance; the union with the declaration's needs is asked.
- **GATE-215** (agent): Every submitted form goes to the sink rule only: asked when a value typed or chosen into that tab carries the owner's private data by provenance, after outside content was read, to the form's action host (else the page's) that the owner neither named in this request nor approved. A submit with no private value never asks (GET or POST) and never raises the new-recipient question.
- **GATE-216** (agent): A browser payment's Yes is keyed to its tab chain (the first task tab that opened it). A Mac app's payment is scoped to its app window (bundle + window id) for 10 minutes; a payment with neither asks every run, showing an unread amount unless the capability describes it. The worker's declared amount is never shown or keyed. Bank page = the tab moved to another host, or the input is in a frame of another host (a payment gateway's card frame too: only a differing amount/merchant asks there).
- **GATE-217** (agent): Complete (next payment asks): a call ran on another host and the chain came back to the checkout's host; a second card form is submitted there; or a one-click paying submit with no card form or bank page before it. Amounts compare by currency and number (a side with no currency compares the number); merchants case- and space-insensitively; an amount read where the approved one was unread asks again. Approvals live in memory (a restart asks again); a No is keyed by chain + amount + merchant and stays final.
- **GATE-218** (agent): KnownDestinations.approved (answered or confirmed) is the sink rule's test; known (any how) stays the new-recipient and outside-value test. A named destination is upgraded when the owner later approves it, never downgraded. Stored keys and values: the text when the redactor leaves it alone, sha256:<digest> when it would change it without a specific hit, never stored or matched when Redactor.hit finds a saved secret or credential format.
- **GATE-219** (agent): Owner secrets saved from a card field keep their kind and fill only a field of the same kind; a card field takes only an entry of its kind or a one-time hidden input. The gateway refuses typed text into a card field and a Luhn-valid card number typed anywhere.
- **GATE-220** (agent): An exception from a tool counts as failed (retry not blocked, the owner's Yes released) when it is Refused (any subclass), a pydantic ValidationError, or carries attempted = False; anything else is unknown for the repeat check (P19). The call's span is finished whatever escapes.
- **GATE-221** (agent): Each confirm.Need carries `reaches` (the target it was decided for: the call's, a fact's, a counted folder) and StandingPermissions.covers compares the scope's site and recipients with that target; tool, identity, account and content stay the call's.
- **GATE-222** (agent): mac.applescript addressed to a web browser (the one browser list) takes the same foreground question as Mac input there (same key: one Yes covers the browser for the task whichever Mac tool acts); a quoted browser page address in the script (chrome://extensions…) asks every time like input on that page. Not refused.
- **GATE-223** (agent): MacAppleScript.file_paths reports each quoted POSIX path and HFS path on a mounted volume as a change, so the one gateway file check applies: FERB's own state, FERB.app and its service definitions refused whatever the owner said, a listed place asks per call.
- **GATE-224** (agent): protection.BROWSER_STORES is browsers.data_folders(): each Chromium browser's user-data folder and the other browsers' data (Safari and its container, Firefox, makers' shared folders). An older config.toml gets each default it was never offered once (journal config.defaults_added), so the owner's own entries and removals stay.
- **GATE-225** (owner): Every question card shows one question. A confirmation's is built by code from its needs with the facts that decide it (the app and how long the Yes lasts, the exact command, amount and merchant, path and count, recipients and text, the profile, a value and its source), plus the task's reason as one small line; the step and raw call stay only in the record. A retry asks in plain words. A task's question carries a structural "from the task" tag instead of a text prefix.
- **GATE-501** (owner): A secret pasted into the chat is masked before any model sees it (every format in the named table plus saved secret values) and the message still runs. FERB adds one reminder under it naming each kind once: it hid it from the AI and didn't save it, and keys and passwords are best not pasted into chats. A saved secret is named as one of the owner's saved secrets. No advice to revoke: the value never left the Mac.
- **GATE-502** (agent): The notice comes from the redactor's finding, never from a model, so it always appears; it names kinds, never the value. The owner's bubble shows the masked text (the ack's message), also after a restart; the journal records chat.secret_hidden with kinds only; the planner gets the hidden kinds as one fact, so a reply never asks the owner to paste it again. The kinds are formats, not intent (AGENTS.md rule 4): nothing is refused.
- **GATE-503** (owner): FERB may write the clipboard and may approve another agent's prompts (owner 2026-10-07: "no, let it do this").
- **GATE-504** (owner): The front window (topmost non-FERB window) is screenshotted, redacted, with every message for the planner and reused by the worker; browser windows, task tabs and recording frames go redacted; an image is withheld only when masking fails; excluded sites are captured as excluded, excluded apps are not looked at or named; never the whole desktop.
- **GATE-505** (agent): A protection-list entry that is another app's container or inside one (~/Library/Containers/<id>, ~/Library/Group Containers/<id>, as typed or under those folders resolved) is never stat'ed, resolved or opened: its resolved form is the containers folder resolved plus the rest as written, it counts as a folder for the shell profile, and a folder above it inside a container is denied as present. - **GATE-506** (agent): The browser URL sink (sink:private_url) does not count a value whose every private occurrence is inside a URL of the destination's host (as before) or in a record read from the destination's own site: a record whose outside labels are only web pages of hosts the destination covers (same host, www aside, or a host under it; never a sibling) plus at most the private label. A value also found anywhere else in private text (a file, another site's page, FERB's context, a mixed record) still counts. Read order (N1), followed links and decoded words (N2) are unchanged.
- **GATE-507** (agent): sink:private_url says which value of the owner's the address would send (the matched token, and the address piece it rides in when that differs, e.g. a decoded or embedded value) and where this task first read it (a file by path, a tool result by tool and site, or the context FERB gave the model), from span facts only, never the record's content beyond the value.
- **GATE-508** (agent): Argument provenance (S3) lists `private` for a value found in a tool result of the tree whose labels are only the private label (and the owner's): a file, an app, nothing outside. S4(b) (sink:outside_value) asks only when a value came only from outside content: not when it is in the owner's words, answers or such a result. - **GATE-509** (agent): The browser and Mac typing tools record a typed email address or phone number as the call's recipient (provenance.typed_destination), never a URL: a URL addresses no one. - **GATE-510** (owner): A task's safety check (confirmation, retry, conversation scope) shows its options and a box "Or tell the task something else" (chat.correct). - **GATE-511** (agent): confirm.pair_need takes the profile's signed-in account (GatewayDeps.profile_account, read fresh) into its values, and the question and its short form say it in brackets after the profile's name. - **GATE-512** (agent): Approval.option_for counts an option's number only for a task's own question. - **GATE-513** (owner): Refines GATE-225's card. A password question still starts with its place. A kind without new words keeps today's sentence; a card that can't be built asks with today's line. The full question stays in the record.
- **GATE-514** (agent): For GATE-513, after the owner asked a fresh agent to review the wording: a card whose Yes makes a person or site known for good (SQ6, GATE-205) says so; sharing data names the value sent; a new site says the task read your own data; the code box holds only the value (its source goes in the why); terminal cards name the app once and say a Yes covers one input; payments say they take money, and a different bank amount says it differs.
- **GATE-515** (agent): History lines (task answers, FERB's replies and questions written from outside content, notices) show origin.shown: the stored labels, except that a record with more than one outside label shows each outside kind once (external:web), never the hosts and senders it inherited; one outside label keeps its detail. A tool result's footer names what the tool itself read with its detail, and labels passed through from FERB's records (chat.history, memory.read, task.evidence) that way. Outside entries stay marked and quoted as data. Display only: stored labels and every check are unchanged.
- **GATE-516** (owner): The sink question is not asked for an address or form that carries only part of one of the owner's private values (for example the last 6 digits of their phone); the whole value still asks, however it is written.
- **GATE-517** (agent): Texts give value forms: tokens, grouped values (digit groups joined by single spaces) and spellings (no separators or case; the owner's digits without grouping separators, never across letters; a phone's national 0 form). A token only inside a grouped value is a part (GATE-516). A URL piece, decoded up to twice more, matches by itself, a spelling, a grouped value in it, or several words written so around a whole value; all groups in separate pieces match. Order, owner and same-site rules apply. Unchanged: one value amid other words; a postcode alone still asks.
- **GATE-518** (agent): Refines GATE-516 and GATE-517 (the coordinator's ruling). In a grouped value, every run of two or more neighbouring groups is a whole value: sent spaced, joined, or each group in its own piece in the value's order, and after a leading + its groups with a 0 or without (the national number is the whole phone; a compact +number tries country codes of 1-3 digits). Only one group sent alone is a part. Groups are never joined across letters, a time or decimal (13:27, 4.5) ends a group, and groups together shorter than MIN_LEN are no value. Matched in linear time per text.
- **GATE-519** (agent): A reply, question, task answer, summary, step note, part or task root stores its sources' kinds (origin.kinds), never their hosts and senders; replies, answers and summaries also store, in their JSON, each owner value their text holds with its classes (carried.derive: owner, private, site:host). - **GATE-520** (owner): Refines GATE-513 for FERB's secret question. The heading stays short and generic with the place first. Under it, the page's own label for the field says what to type, whole and quoted as the page's words (printable, invisible and reordering marks dropped); with no label, the AI's name for it does. The AI's name is shown whole (its character allowlist kept), without a leading copy of the place, cut only past 200 characters. Workers are asked for short names.
- **GATE-522** (agent): For a stored record of FERB's conversation (a context exposure with per-entry segments, GATE-519) the sink's list of the owner's data takes each entry whose whole text counts (the owner's messages, notices, older rows) when its kinds are the owner's words or data, and of each entry FERB wrote only its stored values. - **GATE-527** (agent): Refines GATE-516/517/518 (sink review F1). - **GATE-544** (agent): For GATE-543. - **GATE-548** (agent): A Keychain item trusts the binary that created it. Created by FERB's Python, which runs any script, that trust would be wide; created by `security`, any program running it reads the item. So one small pinned, signed helper (ferb-secrets) creates and reads FERB's items: generic tools now get a Keychain prompt. Limits: the helper checks no caller, so any program running as the owner can ask it for a secret; FERB.app-only store/delete RPCs, the sandbox keeping models, tasks and the shell away from the Keychain and ~/.ferb, and no key in an environment, log or span are what is enforced.
- **GATE-550** (owner): Each test-run task runs in its own chat tagged with its run and connection. - **GATE-557** (agent): For GATE-558, refining GATE-215/514. - **GATE-558** (owner): GATE-537 stays: a site FERB found itself (a search for what the owner described) is not named. Sending the owner's private data there in a form keeps the sink question, asked once per site per task, with a card that names the data, the site and what the click does.
- **GATE-559** (agent): Applies GATE-513 and GATE-520 to login codes. A login-code card's detail quotes the page's own label for the field (the fill's ActionFacts.control_label, page words with GATE-520's display rules) before what happens to the code; a login-code and a secret card carry the fill call's `why` as the small why line, as confirmations do (D33: marked when it reads like FERB's). A fresh ask after the page refused the last value starts its detail with that fact and the page's words (GATE-562). A payment's code card keeps GATE-204's. Display only.
- **GATE-560** (agent): Rule 5. Before any question the gateway runs a capability's `unavailable(args)` hook: mac.applescript reads macOS's Automation answer without a prompt; when it is denied, the call returns the fact (needs_permission, asked_owner false) and nobody is asked. Not asked yet keeps today's order (the owner's Yes, then macOS's prompt); no answer in time leaves `_run`'s check. Refines GATE-201: a name no running app has is keyed by the installed app's bundle id (`apps.installed_bundle`), so a Yes covers an app that quit and reopened.
- **GATE-561** (agent): For GATE-564. Confirmation cards and lines, the why line, hidden-input cards and questions, a retry's card and quoted question redact each inserted value by itself (Gateway.value) and mark the finished text redacted (Gateway.built), so the record, events and chat.status keep FERB's words whole. The mark is the redactor's own, trusted only under the current known values. A retry line whose ledger targets sit inside its sentence is still redacted whole.
- **GATE-562** (agent): For GATE-563. After a sealed browser fill and a form submit on a tab, the tab's next read showing the same page (host, path) with the same field (kind, else label) empty is a refusal; no page word decides it. The read carries the fact for the worker; the owner is told at once in chat, quoting the page's text new since the fill (page origin); the next card for that field says so. After ASKS_AFTER_REFUSAL fresh asks since the first refusal, an ask is refused with the page's words: stop and report. In memory per tree.
- **GATE-563** (owner): When a page refuses a password, login code or card detail FERB filled (it asks for the same field again or shows an error), FERB records it, tells the owner at once with the page's own words, and the next question for it says the last one was refused. After a refusal FERB asks the owner again for the same field at most twice in one task; then that step stops and FERB reports what the page said.
- **GATE-565** (owner): FERB does not read one-time login codes from the owner's inbox to fill them, sealed or not; it asks the owner for the code, with the clearer card (GATE-559).
- **GATE-566** (owner): Reviewed: private-url, new-destination, outside-value typed/recipient/amount, new-recipient(+unseen), bulk-send/delete, pay, account-security, terminal-type/run/paste/key/applescript/other, runnable-file, foreground-script, browser-page, pair-profile, tls-off, protected-read/change, admin/service-lift, retry, secret-one-time/save, login-code, otp, mac-password, which-question, paused-mention, loop-closed-tab, runtime-switch, conversation-scope, forget, downloads-cap, browsing, app-chrome. Unchanged: planner-clarify, worker-question, foreground, delete-permanent, plan-ask, closed-tab, check-in.
- **GATE-567** (agent): For GATE-566. A card's `labels` are its buttons' words; options and recorded answers stay Yes/No (and the 30-minute one); the app answers by number and a typed option or button word picks it (option_for, GATE-512). Headers come from structure; a routine card's 30-minute button carries what it covers. The send-data card says where values were read and the page that named the site, not the outside list (refines GATE-557). Closest truthful words: terminal cards keep which terminal; login code and saved-secret words keep the place before any code word (review M4).
- **GATE-568** (owner): Only pages that need the owner's sign-in to show their content (mail, accounts, documents) count as the owner's private data. A public page read in the owner's signed-in profile (search results, shops, news, Hacker News) does not.
- **GATE-570** (owner): A value that is part of the destination's own host name reveals nothing to that site; sending it there doesn't ask.
- **GATE-571** (agent): For GATE-570. The labels of the destination's host (and their spellings) count as known to that site only when the task read that host before: a page of it, or its name written in what it read. A host that never appeared (VALUE.attacker.example, N3) still asks.
- **GATE-572** (owner): Supersedes GATE-210, GATE-213 and GATE-564, keeping the address-code exemption, CODE_REACH 8 and that FERB's fixed wording is never scanned (inserted values are redacted each by itself). Only FERB's own API keys and tokens are looked for by their value. No saved Keychain secret and nothing typed into FERB's hidden input (passwords, answers, login codes, the Mac password) is searched for in other text. Secret formats, secret fields and the sealed fill path stay. In GATE-501 a known value is one of those keys.
- **GATE-573** (agent): For GATE-572. The registry (sanitize/known.py) holds only API keys (preloaded at start for the runtimes in use, added when read or stored), the egress proxy's per-command tokens and the Claude sign-in code; no saved secret is read for it. Values match exactly, never as words (SealedWord, the word list and the ordinary-word line are gone). Hidden-input values go to their fill only, never leased or remembered; a failure while one is handled is journaled without its message. Test daemons never preload.
- **GATE-575** (owner): Refines GATE-204 and GATE-216 for the payment card only. When code read no amount on the page and the AI declared one, the card's question and exact line show that amount, marked as the AI's that FERB couldn't confirm on the page
